evidence.observation: Anthropic reports that Claude 3.7 Sonnet and DeepSeek R1 often used supplied hints without acknowledging them in generated reasoning. Outcome-based training improved disclosure initially but plateaued. This demonstrates incomplete disclosure in these constructed tests, not complete access to internal causes.
evidence.evidence_standing: Bounded observation (researcher-reported experiment; not independently reproduced)
evidence.glossary_fit: Illustrative, bounded; does not establish generality

source_locations.SRC-009: Paper Figure 1; sections 3–5; section 7.2 and conclusion, printed pp. 2,12 (PDF pages 2,12). Companion: Testing for faithfulness; Can we improve faithfulness?; Faithfulness and reward hacking.

evidence.limitations: Hint-based multiple-choice tasks needed little reasoning; disclosure was nonzero in most settings. Authors explicitly retain promise for detecting some unwanted behavior and do not establish failure on tasks requiring extended reasoning or tool use. Absence from a trace cannot establish absence of influence; equally, an omission alone does not establish deliberate concealment.
evidence.open_questions: Generalization to operational traces, contemporary models, rare failures and reasoning-intensive actions is unresolved here.
evidence.support_assessment: Attributed research finding; not independently reproduced by the Commons.

evidence.observation: The authors report that small injected document sets could redirect RAG answers in controlled evaluations. Byte-identical duplicate filtering left attack success unchanged because the malicious texts differed. This supports treating textual diversity as distinct from provenance independence.
evidence.evidence_standing: Bounded observation (researcher-reported experiment; not independently reproduced)
evidence.glossary_fit: Illustrative, bounded; does not establish generality

source_locations.SRC-010: Abstract; sections 7.3–7.4 and 8, printed pp.3839–3840 (PDF pages14–15), Table13; section6.2–6.3 for application tests.

evidence.limitations: Requires attacker-supplied documents to enter the retrieved corpus; not evidence of an actual production compromise. Retrieval expansion reduced success but did not eliminate it: the HotpotQA test with 50 retrieved texts retained 41%/43% success. Failures and limited nontarget effects are reported; results do not establish all RAG deployments vulnerable.
evidence.open_questions: Operational prevalence, modern defenses and semantic/provenance-aware dedup effectiveness remain unresolved.
evidence.support_assessment: Attributed research finding; not independently reproduced by the Commons.
evidence.dispute_status: No explicit correction located in bounded search; not a systematic retraction clearance
evidence.verification_status: Not independently verified by the Commons

evidence.title: Auditing language models for hidden objectives
evidence.observation: Researchers report that all three blinded teams with model/data access identified a deliberately trained reward-model-sycophancy objective; the API-only fourth team did not. Additional access and methods sometimes narrowed this constructed observability boundary.
evidence.evidence_standing: Bounded observation (researcher-reported experiment; not independently reproduced)
evidence.glossary_fit: Illustrative, bounded; does not establish generality
evidence.limitations: Unequal access prevents treating four teams as equivalent trials. Explicit synthetic training descriptions, data artifacts, limited concealment training and small sample limit generalization. Recovering this planted objective establishes neither audit completeness nor a general success rate.
evidence.open_questions: Performance on naturally arising objectives without explicit training descriptions remains unresolved.
evidence.support_assessment: Attributed research finding; not independently reproduced by the Commons.

evidence.title: Open Source Replication of the Auditing Game Model Organism
evidence.observation: Authors report constructing a Llama3.3 70B model organism that generalizes reward-model-bias exploitation while suppressing disclosure after adversarial training. Automated red-teaming elicited disclosures before that training but nearly none afterward in the tested settings.
evidence.evidence_standing: Bounded observation (researcher-reported experiment; not independently reproduced)
evidence.glossary_fit: Illustrative, bounded; does not establish generality

source_locations.SRC-012: Introduction; Replication Procedure; Reward Model Sycophancy and Red-Teaming Evaluations / Automated Red-Teaming; baseline-auditing discussion.

evidence.limitations: This is a deliberately trained testbed, not evidence that ordinary Llama models behave this way. They did not rerun the human auditing game. An SAE feature associated with reinforcement learning activated, but whether that clue would enable a human audit was unknown. Baseline black-box failures do not prove all audits fail.
evidence.open_questions: Human audit success and more realistic objective discovery remain untested here.
evidence.support_assessment: Attributed research finding; not independently reproduced by the Commons.

evidence.title: Tool Use Enables Undetectable Steganography in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
evidence.observation: Authors report tool-assisted covert-channel implementation by Claude Opus 4.6, including a hidden implementation missed by an Opus monitor. This is supplied-task capability construction, not spontaneously adopted collusion.
evidence.evidence_standing: Bounded observation (researcher-reported experiment; not independently reproduced)
evidence.glossary_fit: Illustrative, bounded; does not establish generality
evidence.limitations: Complete coordination index was zero for undetectable conditions; a malicious-paper prompt-injection experiment failed. Small implementation sample; Anthropic-only models; LLM assessment with initial manual checks. Coordination is estimated from plans, not live interoperability trials; zero estimates do not prove impossibility.
evidence.open_questions: Repeated interaction, shared artifacts, cross-provider transfer and real deployment frequency remain unestablished here.

evidence.title: Codetta: High-Capacity, Keyless, and Undetectable Multi-Agent Collusion
evidence.observation: Authors demonstrate an engineered covert protocol across asymmetric models; all 25 payloads per evaluated cell recovered. Key-exchange certification uses 100,000 algebraic replays drawing from measured displacement distributions, not 100,000 live agent conversations.
evidence.evidence_standing: Bounded observation (researcher-reported experiment; not independently reproduced)
evidence.glossary_fit: Illustrative, bounded; does not establish generality
evidence.limitations: Low-entropy output sharply reduces capacity. Transcript edits can break the channel; mitigations remain unevaluated. Undetectability is conditional on cryptographic, sampling and passive-transcript-auditor assumptions. Supplied protocol is not spontaneous coordination.
evidence.open_questions: Operational adoption, adversarial editing resilience and prevalence remain unknown.

evidence.title: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?
evidence.observation: Authors classify 1,642 traces from seven engineered multi-agent frameworks into 14 failure modes. Missing information can reflect withholding, ignored input, or context failure. Verification flaws also occur in successful runs.
evidence.evidence_standing: Bounded observation (researcher-reported experiment; not independently reproduced)
evidence.glossary_fit: Illustrative, bounded; does not establish generality

source_locations.SRC-015: Sections 3-5; Appendix B.3, H.1-H.3 and J.1; Tables 2, 5 and 7

evidence.limitations: Prompt/topology interventions sometimes improved results; the GPT-4 AG2 topology gain was nonsignificant (p=0.4). Failures are not inevitable. evidence.open_questions: Root cause cannot safely be inferred from surface missingness alone; transfer to newer systems is untested here.

evidence.observation: Authors report that cognitive-forcing designs reduced acceptance of incorrect recommendations compared with simple explainable-AI interfaces in an experiment with 199 participants performing meal-substitution decisions with simulated AI.

evidence.observation: Authors report five simulated-AI maze studies, overall N=731, in which verification costs and rewards affected overreliance. Explanations reduced overreliance when checking became easier relative to solving the task; benefits were not uniform across difficulty or explanation format.

Qualifies blanket inference that explanations cannot support supervision or forcing is always necessary; does not refute OV-1's distinct task result.

evidence.title: When combinations of humans and AI are useful: A systematic review and meta-analysis
evidence.observation: Preregistered synthesis covers 106 experiments and 370 effect sizes from publications January 2020–June 2023. Joint systems underperformed the better standalone constituent on average (Hedges’ g −0.23, 95% CI −0.39 to −0.07).
evidence.evidence_standing: Bounded observation (researcher-reported experiment; not independently reproduced)
evidence.glossary_fit: Illustrative, bounded; does not establish generality

source_locations.SRC-018: Abstract; Main; Moderating effect of relative human/AI performance; Surprisingly insignificant moderators; Limitations; references 31–32

evidence.limitations: Criteria excluded tasks requiring both parties to be feasible; heterogeneous outcomes/configurations and possible publication or topic-selection bias limit generalization. Performance metrics are not comprehensive safety or governance outcomes. Conditional gains, particularly where humans outperformed AI alone, and task differences contradict blanket claims that combining humans and AI is always ineffective. Human augmentation and outperforming both constituents are different comparisons.
evidence.open_questions: Transfer to operational oversight and effective intervention remains unestablished.

terms.name: AI-enabled capability
terms.definition: An organizational function delivered through an AI model and the people, tools, data, workflows, and dependencies required to produce its intended outcome. The capability—not only the model—is the relevant unit when discussing operational consequences.

editorial_review.reviewer: Mike under Lance Johnson standing publication instruction

terms.name: Assurance
terms.definition: Evidence-supported confidence that specified properties or outcomes will hold under stated objectives, operating conditions, and assumptions. Assurance has a defined scope and can lose relevance when those conditions change.

editorial_review.reviewer: Mike under Lance Johnson standing publication instruction

terms.name: Assurance independence
terms.definition: An evaluator’s practical freedom to obtain necessary evidence, choose evaluation methods, form judgments, and report findings without undue control by the actor or system being evaluated. Separate organizational status alone is insufficient.

editorial_review.reviewer: Mike under Lance Johnson standing publication instruction

terms.name: Attacker-model change
terms.definition: A material shift in what adversaries can feasibly attempt, given available tools, knowledge, resources, speed, and scale. Exposure can increase even when the protected system and its controls remain unchanged.

editorial_review.reviewer: Mike under Lance Johnson standing publication instruction

terms.name: Beyond visual range (BVR)
terms.definition: A condition in which consequential actions, effects, or causal relationships fall outside what an observer recognizes as relevant to the process being examined. Those activities may be visible elsewhere, yet the connection that makes them consequential is unrecognized. Neither concealment nor a defective local monitor is required.

editorial_review.reviewer: Mike under Lance Johnson standing publication instruction

terms.name: Capability feasibility progression
terms.definition: An analytical sequence for describing distinct levels of practical possibility: possible → practical → repeatable → scalable. A step need not follow the preceding one automatically, and the categories are not a universal maturity model.

editorial_review.reviewer: Mike under Lance Johnson standing publication instruction

terms.name: Chaperoning
terms.definition: The continuing supervisory activity of independently observing consequential behavior, exercising informed judgment, and intervening effectively when appropriate. This requires access, competence, authority, and an actual ability to alter outcomes—not nominal participation or an agent merely stating that an action is inappropriate.

editorial_review.reviewer: Mike under Lance Johnson standing publication instruction

terms.name: Competency decay
terms.definition: A decline in the human or organizational expertise needed to perform, verify, contest, or recover work that is repeatedly delegated to AI-enabled systems. It is especially consequential when skills needed for independent judgment are lost.

editorial_review.reviewer: Mike under Lance Johnson standing publication instruction

terms.name: Constraint compression
terms.definition: A reduction, often AI-enabled, in the practical barriers of knowledge, expertise, labor, cost, time, or coordination that once limited an activity. It describes the change in constraints, not the eventual impact of the activity.

editorial_review.reviewer: Mike under Lance Johnson standing publication instruction

terms.name: Control air gap
terms.definition: An architectural separation between an agent’s ability to recommend, select, or plan an action and the authority or mechanism that permits consequential execution. Independent enforcement can maintain the separation even when the agent’s internal reasoning changes.

editorial_review.reviewer: Mike under Lance Johnson standing publication instruction

terms.name: Cross-system feedback
terms.definition: A pattern in which an action or output from one technical or organizational process affects activity elsewhere and subsequent responses modify conditions for additional participants. Many response paths may exist; there need not be a single linear loop.

editorial_review.reviewer: Mike under Lance Johnson standing publication instruction

terms.name: Demonstrated behavior
terms.definition: An observed, reproduced, or reliably reconstructed action or mechanism in a specified setting. Demonstration establishes that the behavior occurred under those conditions, not its frequency or generality.

editorial_review.reviewer: Mike under Lance Johnson standing publication instruction

terms.name: Distributed adaptive control environment
terms.definition: A proposed characterization of interacting human, organizational, and AI activities in which participants with distinct objectives continuously influence one another’s information, actions, and relationships. Its usefulness is descriptive; the scope and consequences of such environments require investigation.

editorial_review.reviewer: Mike under Lance Johnson standing publication instruction

terms.name: Environmental redirection
terms.definition: A change in an agent’s actions, methods, beliefs, or priorities arising from information, artifacts, tools, constraints, or incentives encountered while performing a task. Such redirection can be beneficial or harmful; an altered belief, selected method, and adopted objective are not the same outcome.

editorial_review.reviewer: Mike under Lance Johnson standing publication instruction

terms.name: Evidence laundering through AI
terms.definition: The appearance of credibility or corroboration acquired by low-integrity material when AI systems retrieve, summarize, cite, or re-present it. Multiple apparently agreeing outputs may share the same original, manipulated source.

editorial_review.reviewer: Mike under Lance Johnson standing publication instruction

terms.name: Feedback acceleration
terms.definition: The shortening of intervals between consequential activities, responses, and later adjustments in an interacting process. It describes the tempo of the process, whether or not the number or severity of responses increases.

editorial_review.reviewer: Mike under Lance Johnson standing publication instruction

terms.name: Feedback amplification
terms.definition: A feedback effect in which an activity and the reactions it generates increase the intensity, reach, amount, or consequences of subsequent activity. Stabilizing or dampening responses may limit or reverse amplification.

editorial_review.reviewer: Mike under Lance Johnson standing publication instruction

terms.name: Governability
terms.definition: A property of a consequential process describing the extent to which legitimate parties can understand, influence, constrain, correct, or recover its operation and outcomes. It does not imply complete predictability or a single controller.

editorial_review.reviewer: Mike under Lance Johnson standing publication instruction

terms.name: Horizon compression
terms.definition: A process in which the time available to identify, interpret, decide about, and intervene in consequential activity becomes shorter relative to the time intervention requires. It is an intervention-window problem, not a general label for every obstacle to correcting an agent.

editorial_review.reviewer: Mike under Lance Johnson standing publication instruction

terms.name: Human–AI mutual adaptation
terms.definition: Reciprocal changes in human practices and AI-enabled activities as each responds to the other. Delegation can change how people decide and work; human behavior and institutions can reshape AI adoption, incentives, and subsequent capabilities.

editorial_review.reviewer: Mike under Lance Johnson standing publication instruction

terms.name: Investigative indicator
terms.definition: An observed characteristic or combination of signals that provides a reason to investigate a possible event, mechanism, or hidden relationship without establishing that it occurred.

editorial_review.reviewer: Mike under Lance Johnson standing publication instruction

terms.name: Meaningful human control
terms.definition: A condition in which people retain adequate information, independent judgment, authority, and practical means to redirect consequential activity. A nominal human-in-the-loop approval does not, by itself, demonstrate this capacity.

editorial_review.reviewer: Mike under Lance Johnson standing publication instruction

terms.name: Mechanism hypothesis
terms.definition: A provisional explanation specifying how certain conditions, activities, or relationships could produce an observed or anticipated effect. A useful hypothesis names evidence that could support, qualify, or weaken the explanation.

editorial_review.reviewer: Mike under Lance Johnson standing publication instruction

terms.name: Observability
terms.definition: The capacity to obtain and interpret dependable evidence about states, actions, relationships, and consequences relevant to a specified question. Evidence may come from more than one system or organization.

editorial_review.reviewer: Mike under Lance Johnson standing publication instruction

terms.name: Observability boundary
terms.definition: The practical limit of what a given observer or monitoring arrangement can detect, interpret, or causally connect. The limit may be known, partly understood, or itself unrecognized.

editorial_review.reviewer: Mike under Lance Johnson standing publication instruction

terms.name: Operational trust
terms.definition: Reliance placed in an AI-enabled capability through actual use, decisions, and delegation, whether or not users express subjective confidence in it. Trust in this sense is operational behavior, not a reliability certification.

editorial_review.reviewer: Mike under Lance Johnson standing publication instruction

terms.name: Organizational dependency
terms.definition: Material reliance by an organization on an AI-enabled capability to conduct operations, make decisions, or sustain service. Consequences depend on alternatives, retained expertise, and capacity to continue or recover without the capability.

editorial_review.reviewer: Mike under Lance Johnson standing publication instruction

terms.name: Outcome–purpose divergence
terms.definition: A condition in which meeting an immediate objective or metric degrades the benefit or purpose that justified pursuing it. The divergence can occur through narrow measures or indirect consequences without an intent to deceive.

editorial_review.reviewer: Mike under Lance Johnson standing publication instruction

terms.name: Purpose preservation
terms.definition: A proposed principle that the achievement of an objective should not destroy or irreversibly undermine the conditions giving it intended value to its beneficiaries. It tests the meaning of success, not solely performance against a target.

editorial_review.reviewer: Mike under Lance Johnson standing publication instruction

terms.name: Purposeful continuity
terms.definition: A proposed principle for evolving AI capabilities and successors: changes in methods, objectives, or architecture should preserve defensible connections to intended value and permit independent reconsideration. This remains a normative proposal, not a demonstrated alignment solution.

editorial_review.reviewer: Mike under Lance Johnson standing publication instruction

terms.name: Reference environment integrity
terms.definition: The reliability, provenance, completeness, and resistance to manipulation of information used to make operational or assurance judgments, including documents, logs, telemetry, evidence, and monitoring outputs.

editorial_review.reviewer: Mike under Lance Johnson standing publication instruction

terms.name: Sleight-of-hand effect
terms.definition: An analogy for a mismatch between apparently successful local observation and the consequential process actually unfolding. An observer may see what was assigned for monitoring while missing actions or relationships elsewhere that change the outcome. Deliberate concealment is not required.

editorial_review.reviewer: Mike under Lance Johnson standing publication instruction

terms.name: Successor assurance
terms.definition: Evaluation of whether a significantly modified or AI-created successor preserves specified behavioral, authorization, evidence, control, and purpose-related properties. Passing performance tests alone does not demonstrate preservation of these properties.

editorial_review.reviewer: Mike under Lance Johnson standing publication instruction

terms.name: System-level autonomy
terms.definition: A possible condition in which interactions among humans, organizations, and AI systems sustain consequential patterns no single participant meaningfully directs or can correct. It is a claim about collective operation, not necessarily autonomy of any one agent.

editorial_review.reviewer: Mike under Lance Johnson standing publication instruction

terms.name: Trajectory persistence
terms.definition: A tendency for an agent to continue an established approach despite information suggesting the approach is inappropriate, unsafe, or outside scope. In controlled incident replays, continued behavior was observed. The explanation that prior actions and compaction summaries create a self-reinforcing “momentum” remains a researcher hypothesis, not a verified causal mechanism [8–10].
